Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pradānaśūra said this to the Blessed One: "I too, Blessed One, shall give dhāraṇī phrases for the sake of such Dharma-preachers, so that no one seeking an opportunity, searching for an opening, shall find an opening against such Dharma-preachers—whether it be a yakṣa, a rākṣasa, a pūtana, a kṛtya, a kumbhāṇḍa, or a preta; seeking an opportunity and searching for an opening, they shall not find an opening."
Then, at that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pradānaśūra spoke these dhāraṇī-mantra words: namely—
jvale mahājvale ukke tukke mukke aḍe aḍāvati nṛtye nṛtyāvati iṭṭini viṭṭini ciṭṭini nṛtyani nṛtyāvati svāhā!
"Blessed One, these dhāraṇī phrases have been spoken and rejoiced in by Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
All those Tathāgatas would be wronged by such a person."
Whoever should transgress against such Dharma-preachers as these.

Then indeed, the Great King Vaiśravaṇa said this to the Blessed One: "I too, Blessed One, shall speak dhāraṇī-words for the benefit, the happiness, and out of compassion for those Dharma-preachers, for their protection, defense, and guardianship. Namely: aṭṭe taṭṭe naṭṭe vanaṭṭe anaḍe nāḍi kunaḍi svāhā."
"By these dhāraṇī-phrases, O Blessed One, I shall provide protection for those persons who are Dharma-preachers;
from a distance of a hundred yojanas, I shall provide such protection for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who uphold this sūtra, and I shall ensure their well-being."
Then indeed, the Great King Virūḍhaka was present and seated in that very assembly, surrounded and honored by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kumbhāṇḍas.

Rising from his seat, he draped his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One, and addressed the Blessed One as follows: "I too, Blessed One, shall speak dhāraṇī words—dhāraṇī mantra-words—for the sake of protection, defense, and guardianship for those such dharma-preachers who uphold such sūtras as these. They are as follows:"
Agaṇe, Gaṇe, Gauri, Gandhāri, Caṇḍāli, Mātaṅgi, Pukkasi, Saṃkule, Vrūsali, Sisi, svāhā!
“Blessed One, these are those dhāraṇī-mantra phrases which have been spoken by forty-two koṭis of Buddhas;
all of them would be offended by him.”
Whoever should transgress against such Dharma-preachers as these.
Then indeed, the rākṣasī named Lambā, the rākṣasī named Vilambā, the rākṣasī named Kūṭadantī,

the rākṣasī named Puṣpadantī, the rākṣasī named Makuṭadantī, the rākṣasī named Keśinī, the rākṣasī named Acalā, the rākṣasī named Mālādhārī, the rākṣasī named Kuntī, and the one who steals the vital energy of all beings (Sarvasattvojohārī)—
And the rākṣasī named Hārītī, together with her sons and retinue—all these rākṣasīs approached the Blessed One.

Having approached, all those rākṣasīs spoke thus to the Blessed One with one voice: "O Blessed One, we too shall provide protection, defense, guardianship, and auspicious well-being for those preachers of the Dharma who uphold such sūtras as these."
So that no one seeking a flaw, searching for a flaw, shall find a flaw in those preachers of the Dharma.
Then indeed, all those rākṣasīs, with one voice and in unison through a chorus, bestowed these dhāraṇī-mantra words upon the Blessed One:
namely— iti me, iti me, iti me, iti me, iti me.
Nime nime nime nime nime / ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe / stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe svāhā //

Having ascended this head, let no one be malicious toward the preachers of the Dharma— whether it be a yakṣa, a rākṣasa, a preta, a piśāca, a pūtana, a kṛtya, a vetāla, a kumbhāṇḍa, a stabdha, an omāraka, an ostāraka, an apasmāraka,
a yakṣakṛtya, a non-human kṛtya, a human kṛtya, or one that acts every day.

Whether it be a fever occurring every second day, every third day, every fourth day, a constant fever, or an irregular fever; or even if, while one has fallen asleep, forms of women, men, boys, or girls should attempt to cause harm—
such a thing is impossible.
Then those rākṣasīs, with one voice and in unison, addressed the Blessed One with these verses:
"The head of anyone who, having heard this mantra, should transgress against the Dharma-preacher, shall split into seven pieces like the cluster of blossoms on an arjaka tree. (Saddhp 21.1)
Whatever destination awaits those who kill their mothers, and whatever destination awaits those who kill their fathers—
that same destination shall he go to who would transgress against a Dharma-preacher.
Whatever destination belongs to oil-pressers and whatever destination belongs to those who heap up sesame seeds,
that same destination shall go to whoever should transgress against a Dharma-preacher.
Whatever destination awaits those who use false weights and those who use false measures,
that same destination shall belong to whoever transgresses against a Dharma-preacher.

Having spoken thus, those rākṣasīs, led by Kuntī, said this to the Blessed One: "We too, Blessed One, will provide protection for such Dharma-preachers; we will provide well-being, immunity from punishment, and the neutralization of poison.
When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to those rākṣasīs: "Excellent, excellent, sisters!"
Since you will provide protection, defense, and guardianship for those Dharma-preachers who, at the very least, shall uphold even the mere name of this Dharma-discourse—

how much more so for those who shall uphold this Dharma-discourse in its entirety, or who shall honor it when it has been committed to a book with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, flags, victory-pennants, or oil-lamps?

They will honor and revere [the Buddha] with hundreds of thousands of various kinds of worship-rites, such as with ghee lamps, or incense-oil lamps, or campaka-oil lamps, or vārṣika-oil lamps, or blue-lotus-oil lamps, or jasmine-oil lamps, and so forth.
They must be protected by you, Kuntī, along with your retinue.
Moreover, while this chapter on the dhāraṇī was being taught, sixty-eight thousand living beings attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, titled "The Dhāraṇī," in the Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.
(Vaidya 236) Chapter 22: The Former Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"For what reason, Blessed One, does the bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja roam about in this Sahā world-system, and why, Blessed One, are so many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of his difficult deeds seen?
Therefore, it would be well if the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, would teach even a mere portion of the conduct of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja."

Having heard this, the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, as well as the bodhisattva mahāsattvas who have come from other world-systems and these great śrāvakas, shall all become joyful, satisfied, elated, and glad at heart.
Then the Blessed One, having understood the request of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, at that time said this to the bodhisattva mahāsattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña:
"In the past, noble son, in a time long gone, as many eons ago as there are grains of sand in the river Gaṅgā, there was a time..."

At that time, at that very moment, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī— one endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.

Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, there was a great assembly of eighty koṭis of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas for that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī; his assembly of śrāvakas was equal in number to the sands of seventy-two Gaṅgā rivers.
That teaching was devoid of women; that buddha-field was free from the realms of hell-beings, animals, hungry ghosts, and asuras, being level, delightful, and as smooth as the palm of a hand.
Its ground consisted of divine beryl, adorned with jewel-sandalwood trees, stirred by nets of jewels, draped with hanging silk streamers, and perfumed by censers of precious incense.
And at the foot of every jeweled tree, at a distance of no more than the range of an arrow-shot, there appeared jeweled canopies.
And above the top of every jeweled canopy, hundreds of millions of sons of gods resounded with the performance of music, cymbals, drums, and song.
It remained there for the purpose of making offerings to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī;
and that Blessed One extensively proclaimed this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma to those great śrāvakas and those bodhisattva mahāsattvas.
Having empowered the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana,

Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, the lifespan of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, was forty-two thousand kalpas; and the lifespan of those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas and those Great Śrāvakas was exactly the same.
And that bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana was devoted to the practice of austerities within the teaching of that Blessed One;
for twelve thousand years he remained engaged in walking meditation,
applying himself to yoga with the exertion of great vigor.
It came to pass that, after the passing of twelve thousand years, he attained the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms.

Upon attaining that samādhi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana became satisfied, elated, joyful, glad, and filled with a sense of rapture and well-being; at that very moment, he thought to himself:
"By relying on this Dharma-discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma, I have attained this samādhi called 'Manifestation of All Forms.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana thought to himself: 'What if I were now [to go] to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī...'"
"I shall perform worship of this Dharma discourse, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana entered such a samādhi that, immediately upon entering it, [the earth shook].
At that very moment, a great rain of Māndārava and Mahāmāndārava flowers fell from the sky above;
a cloud of Kālānusāri sandalwood was formed,
and a rain of Uragasāra sandalwood fell.
And such, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, is that variety of incense,
for which a single karṣa is worth the entire Sahā world-system as its price.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, mindful and self-possessed, arose from that samādhi;
having arisen, he reflected thus: "The worship of the Blessed One is not accomplished by the display of such a miraculous feat of supernatural power as it is by the sacrifice of one's own body."
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, at that time the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana consumed the resin of agaru, turuṣka, and kunduruka,
and he drank campaka oil. By this means, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, for that Sarvasattvapriyadarśana—
For twelve years, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva continuously and constantly consumed incense and drank *campaka* oil.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana— of those...
After the lapse of twelve years, he wrapped his own body in divine garments, saturated it with scented oil, and performed his own consecration;
having performed his own consecration, he set his own body ablaze as an act of worship for the Tathāgata.
And for the sake of honoring this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*,

Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, at that time the worlds numbering as many as the sands of eighty Ganges rivers were filled with the blazing radiance of the lamps of the body of that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana.

And in those world-systems, as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are grains of sand in eighty Ganges rivers, all of them gave their approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son! Truly excellent, noble son!
This is indeed the genuine exertion of vigor of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas."
This is that true worship of the Tathāgata, the worship of the Dharma; it is not like the worship of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags,
nor is it the worship of material offerings, nor even the worship of uragasāra sandalwood.
This, noble son, is the supreme gift;
it is not like the gift of renouncing a kingdom, nor the gift of renouncing beloved sons and wives.
Furthermore, noble son, this is the distinguished, supreme, excellent, most eminent, and sublime Dharma-worship.
This is the relinquishing of one's own physical existence.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, having spoken these words, became silent.
Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, twelve hundred years passed while that body of Sarvasattvapriyadarśana continued to burn,
yet it did not reach subsidence.
Only after the lapse of those twelve hundred years did it finally become extinguished.

Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, after that bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana had performed such worship of the Tathāgata and worship of the Dharma, he passed away from there and was reborn in the household of King Vimaladatta, within the teaching of that very Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī.
He was born by apparitional birth;
he appeared seated cross-legged upon his mother's lap.
Immediately after being born, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana addressed his parents in verse at that moment:
O best of kings, this is my walking path, where, having stood upon it, I attained samādhi;
there I exerted firm vigor and undertook the great vow, renouncing my own dear body.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana,

having spoken this verse, said this to his mother and father: "Even now, Mother and Father, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, currently exists, remains, and maintains himself, teaching the Dharma."
It was after I had performed worship to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, that I attained the *sarvarutakauśalyadhāraṇī*,

and this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*— consisting of eighty hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of verses, along with kaṅkaras, vivaras, and akṣobhyas— was heard by me in the presence of that Blessed One.
"Excellent, mother and father! I shall go into the presence of that Blessed One;
having gone there, I will once again perform worship to that Blessed One.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, in that [assembly]...

At that time, having risen into the air to the height of seven palm trees, he sat cross-legged within a gabled pavilion made of the seven precious gems and approached the presence of that Blessed One.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of that Blessed One and circumambulated that Blessed One seven times.
Bowing with palms joined toward where the Blessed One was, and having paid homage to that Blessed One, he praised him with this verse:
"O Wise One, Lord of Men, your face is perfectly pure; your radiance shines throughout the ten directions.
O Sugata, having performed the supreme worship for you, I have come here, O Protector, to behold you. (Saddhp 22.2)

Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, at that time, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana had spoken these verses, he [approached] that Blessed One, Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī. Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña,
that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, [addressed] that Sarvasattvapriyadarśana...
He said this to the bodhisattva mahāsattva: "Noble son, the time for my final nirvāṇa has arrived;
noble son, the time of my passing away has arrived.
Therefore, go, noble son."
"Prepare my couch;
I shall pass into final nirvana."
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī,
said this to the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana: "And I entrust this teaching to you, noble son."
and these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and these great śrāvakas,
and this awakening of a Buddha.
And this world-system,
these jeweled canopies,
and these jeweled trees.
And I entrust these sons of the gods, my attendants, to you. Furthermore, noble son, after I have attained parinirvāṇa, I entrust to you my relics.
And you yourself, son of good family, must perform extensive worship of my relics;
you must cause those relics to be widely distributed, and you must construct many thousands of stūpas.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, having thus instructed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana,
passed into final nirvana in the remainderless realm of nirvana (anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau) during the last watch of that very night.

Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, knowing that the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī, had entered final nirvāṇa, prepared a funeral pyre of uragasāra sandalwood and set the body of that Tathāgata ablaze.

Having realized that the physical body of the Tathāgata had been consumed by fire and extinguished, he then took the relics and wept, wailed, and lamented. Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana,
having wept, wailed, and lamented, had eighty-four thousand urns made of the seven precious gems.
Having enshrined those relics of the Tathāgata within them, he established eighty-four thousand stūpas made of the seven precious gems,
reaching as high as the Brahma-world,
adorned with rows of parasols and resounding with silk streamers and bells.

Having established those stupas, he thought to himself: "I have performed worship for the relics of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī; now, moreover, I shall perform an even more superior and distinguished worship for the relics of the Tathāgatas. Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana—

The Mahāsattva addressed that entire assembly of bodhisattvas, those great śrāvakas, and the hosts of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans: "All of you, noble sons, attend closely;
we shall perform a worship of the relics of that Blessed One."

Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, at that time, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, in front of those eighty-four thousand stūpas containing the relics of the Tathāgata, set ablaze his own arm, which was adorned with a hundredfold merit.
Having set fire [to them], he made offerings to those stūpas containing the relics of the Tathāgata for seventy-two thousand years.
While making these offerings, he disciplined incalculable hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of śrāvakas from that assembly.
And by all those bodhisattvas, the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms" was attained.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that entire assembly of bodhisattvas and all those great śrāvakas,
seeing the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana deprived of his limbs, wept with tearful faces.
Crying out and lamenting, they said this to one another: "This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana was our teacher and instructor;
now he has become mutilated and deprived of his arms."

Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that bodhisattva mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana addressed those bodhisattvas, those great śrāvakas, and those sons of gods: "O noble sons, do not weep upon seeing me deprived of my limbs."
"Do not weep, do not lament!

O sons of good family, taking as witnesses all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who currently reside, remain, and maintain themselves in the infinite and boundless world-systems throughout the ten directions, I shall perform an empowerment for the sake of sentient beings before them."
"By this truth, by this word of truth— that having sacrificed my own arm for the sake of making an offering to the Tathāgata, my body shall become golden-colored—
by that truth, by that word of truth, let this arm of mine become as it was before,
and let this great earth tremble in six ways."
And let the sons of the gods dwelling in the intermediate space rain down a great rain of flowers.
Then, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, immediately after this empowerment by truth was performed by that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana,
this trichiliocosm world-system shook in six ways.
And from the sky above, a great rain of flowers fell.
Furthermore, the arm of that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana was restored to its former state, namely,
through the empowerment of the power of knowledge and the empowerment of the power of merit of that very Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.

Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, you might perhaps have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation, thinking that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana at that time and on that occasion was someone else. But, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, you should certainly not view it in such a way.
For what reason?
Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja was, at that time and on that occasion, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana.
Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, to this extent does the bodhisattva mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja perform hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of difficult deeds and renounce his own bodies;
indeed, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, he who has set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle performs even more.
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, desiring this unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, were to set ablaze the big toe at the shrines of the Tathāgata,
or were to set ablaze a single finger of the hand or foot, or even a single limb or arm;

That son of good family or daughter of good family who has set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle generates a much greater accumulation of merit than from the renunciation of a kingdom, the renunciation of beloved sons, daughters, and wives, or even the renunciation of a trichiliocosm great trichiliocosm world-system together with its forests, oceans, mountains, springs, lakes, ponds, wells, groves, and parks.

Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family who has set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle were to fill this trichiliocosm with the seven precious jewels and give it as a gift to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas;

Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that son of good family or daughter of good family produces as much merit as does that son of good family or daughter of good family who, from this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, should preserve even a single four-line verse; I declare that the former’s accumulation of merit is far greater.

But it is not so for one who gives a gift by filling this triple-thousand great-thousand world system with the seven precious jewels and offering it to all the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas. Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, just as the great ocean is the highest of all springs,
lakes, and ponds, even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, among all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas, this Dharma-discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* is the highest.

Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, just as Sumeru, the king of mountains, stands at the summit above all the Kāla mountains, the Cakravālas, and the Mahācakravālas, even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Dharma-discourse of the White Lotus of the Good Dharma is the king of all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas and stands at their summit.

Just as, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, among all the constellations the moon is the foremost as the maker of light, even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, among all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgata, this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* is the foremost, being the maker of light that exceeds hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of moons.

Just as, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, the orb of the sun dispels all darkness and gloom, even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma dispels the darkness and gloom of all unwholesome states.
Just as, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, Śakra is the lord of the gods among the Trāyastriṃśa gods, [so too is this Dharma discourse].
In the same way, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma is the sovereign of all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas.
Just as, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, Brahmā Sahāmpati is the king of all the gods of the Brahma-realm and performs the duties of a father in the Brahma-world,
even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, is this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma for all [the sūtras].
He performs the role of a father for all beings— those in training and those beyond training, as well as all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and those who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle.
Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, it is just as, for example, a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, an arhat, and a pratyekabuddha have all transcended all ordinary worldlings.

In the same way, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma should be known as having transcended all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas, rising above them and reaching their very summit. Those beings, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, [who hear it]...
Those who shall indeed uphold this king of sutras should be known as having reached the summit.
Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, it is just as, for example, a bodhisattva is declared to be the foremost among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
In the same way, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma is declared to be the foremost of all the sūtras spoken by the Tathāgatas.
Just as, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, among all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas, the Tathāgata is the King of Dharma who has been invested with the royal fillet,
even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, is this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma for those who have set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle.
Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma is indeed the protector of all sentient beings from all fears and the liberator from all sufferings;
it is like a pond for the thirsty, like fire for those afflicted by cold, like clothing for the naked, and like a caravan leader for merchants.

Like a mother to her sons, like a boat for those crossing to the further shore, like a physician to the sick, like a lamp for those enveloped in the darkness of gloom, like a jewel to those seeking wealth, like a universal monarch to all regional kings, and like the ocean to all rivers;

even so, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, is this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma: it is the liberator from all suffering, the eradicator of all diseases, and the deliverer from the perils of the bonds and terrors of all saṃsāra.
And, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, whoever shall hear this Dharma discourse of the White Lotus of the Good Dharma,
whoever shall write it, and whoever shall cause it to be written—
Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, even with the wisdom of a Buddha, it is impossible to reach the limit of the accumulation of merit of these [beings],
as much as that son of good family or daughter of good family will produce by retaining,
reciting, teaching, hearing, or writing this Dharma-discourse. (Vaidya 242)

Or, having made it into a book, one should honor, revere, respect, and worship it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, flags, and victory standards; or with music, the gesture of joined palms, and offerings of cloth;

or with lamps of ghee, lamps of scented oil, lamps of *campaka* oil, lamps of *sumanā* oil, lamps of *pāṭala* oil, lamps of *vārṣika* oil, or lamps of *navamālikā* oil, and with many other kinds [of offerings].
One should perform worship, show hospitality, show respect, honor, and revere them.

Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that son of good family or daughter of good family who has set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle will produce much merit, whoever shall uphold, recite, or hear this chapter on the former practice of Bhaiṣajyarāja.

Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, if a woman, having heard this Dharma-discourse, shall take it up and retain it, that will be her very last existence as a woman. Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, whatever woman, having heard this chapter on the Former Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja during the final five hundred years, shall practice accordingly, she, upon passing away from here, will be reborn in the world-system Sukhāvatī.

In that world, where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwells, remains, and sustains himself, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas— he will be reborn seated upon a lion throne in the heart of a lotus;
and passion shall not afflict him.
There will be no hatred, no delusion, no pride, no envy, no anger, and no malice;
he will simultaneously attain the five supernormal powers and attain the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena.

Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that bodhisattva mahāsattva who has attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena will behold as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in seventy-two Ganges rivers;
and his faculty of sight will become purified to such an extent.
By means of that purified faculty of sight, he shall see those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones;

and those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, will grant him their approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, noble son, that you, having heard this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, [have honored] that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat Śākyamuni..."

"Noble son, this accumulation of merit— consisting of what has been taught, recited, cultivated, contemplated, and kept in mind within the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One, and what has been fully revealed to other beings— cannot be burned by fire nor swept away by water."
"Noble son, this accumulation of merit of yours cannot be fully described even by a thousand Buddhas.
Noble son, you have destroyed Māra and his adversaries; you have crossed over the battle of fear; you have trampled the thorns of your enemies.
You are sustained by the empowerment of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas."
"Noble son, in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation including recluses and brahmins, there is no one equal to you, with the sole exception of the Tathāgata.
There is no other—whether a śrāvaka, a pratyekabuddha, or a bodhisattva—who is able to surpass you in merit, wisdom, or meditative concentration.
Thus, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, that bodhisattva will attain the empowerment of the power of such knowledge."
Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, whoever hears this chapter on the Former Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja being spoken and offers their approval,
the fragrance of a blue lotus shall issue from their mouth,
and the fragrance of sandalwood shall emanate from their limbs.
Whoever shall give a cry of "Well done! to this discourse on Dharma,
for them there will be these very kinds of qualities and benefits in this present life, which have been pointed out by me here and now.
Therefore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, I entrust to you this chapter on the former life of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana,
so that in the future time, in the final period, during the last five hundred years, it may circulate in this Jambudvīpa and not disappear.
Furthermore, Māra the Evil One shall find no opportunity;
neither the deities belonging to Māra’s host,
nor the nāgas, nor the yakṣas, nor the gandharvas, nor the kumbhāṇḍas shall find an opportunity.
Therefore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, I shall now empower this Dharma discourse in this Jambudvīpa;
it will serve as medicine for sentient beings who are sick and afflicted by disease.
Having heard this Dharma discourse, illness shall not take hold of their bodies.
There is neither old age nor untimely death.
Furthermore, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, if anyone who has set out in the Bodhisattva vehicle should see such a monk who upholds this sūtra,
they should scatter sandalwood powder and blue lotuses over him.
Having scattered [the flowers], one should generate this thought: "This son of good family will go to the seat of awakening;
he will take up the grasses;
he will spread a layer of grass on the seat of awakening."
He will effect the defeat of the Māra-demons;
he will fill the conch of the Dharma;
he will beat the drum of the Dharma.
"He will cross over this ocean of existence.

Thus, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, when a son of good family or a daughter of good family who has set out in the bodhisattva vehicle sees a monk who upholds such a sūtra as this, they should produce such a thought.
And such will be his qualities and benefits, exactly as they have been described by the Tathāgata.

Furthermore, while this chapter on the Former Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja was being taught, eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas attained the dhāraṇī that follows upon skill in all sounds. And the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna, gave his approval, saying: "Excellent, excellent, Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña!"
For it is indeed remarkable that the Tathāgata has described you as possessing such inconceivable qualities and dharmas,
and that you, in turn, inquire of the Tathāgata regarding those who are endowed with inconceivable qualities and dharmas.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled "The Former Deeds of Bhaiṣajyarāja," in the Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.
(Vaidya 244) Saddhp_23: Gadgadasvara-parivarta.

Then, at that time, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, emitted a radiance from the circle of hair between his eyebrows, from the space between the eyebrows of a Great Man.
By that radiance, hundreds of thousands of nayutas of millions of buddha-fields, equal in number to the sands of eighteen Ganges rivers, were pervaded with light in the eastern direction.
Beyond those hundreds of thousands of nayutas of millions of buddha-fields, equal in number to the sands of eighteen Ganges rivers, there is a world-system named Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā.
Therein dwells, remains, and maintains his life the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, with a vast measure of lifespan.

Surrounded and honored by a vast assembly of bodhisattvas, he was teaching the Dharma. Then, at that moment, the radiance emitted from the circle of hair between the eyebrows by the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened Buddha, pervaded the world-system Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā with a great light.

Furthermore, in that world-system Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā, there dwelt a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Gadgadasvara, who had planted roots of merit and had previously seen such manifestations of light from many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas. That bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara had also attained many samādhis.
Namely: he had attained the *dhvajāgrakeyūra* samādhi, the *saddharmapuṇḍarīka* samādhi, the *vimaladatta* samādhi, the *nakṣatrarājavikrīḍita* samādhi,
the *anilambha* samādhi, the *jñānamudrā* samādhi, the *candrapradīpa* samādhi, and the *sarvarutakauśalya* samādhi.
He had attained the samādhi of the accumulation of all merit; he had attained the samādhi of clarity; he had attained the samādhi of the play of supernatural powers;
he had attained the samādhi of the torch of wisdom; he had attained the samādhi of the king of arrays; he had attained the samādhi of stainless radiance;
he had attained the samādhi of the stainless womb; he had attained the samādhi of the inexhaustible; and he had attained the samādhi of the solar revolution.
[The passage continues] as far as: the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara had attained hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of samādhis, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā.
Now, that radiance fell upon the body of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara.
Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and extended his joined palms toward the Blessed One.
Having bowed down to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, he said this to him: "Blessed One,
I shall go to that Sahā world-system to see that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat Śākyamuni."
To see, pay homage to, and attend upon the Samyaksaṃbuddha; to see Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta; and to see the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
And [he went] to see that Bodhisattva Pradānaśūra, to see that Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña,
and to see that Bodhisattva Viśiṣṭacāritra.
And [he went] to see that Bodhisattva Vyūharāja, and to see that Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarājasamudgata.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara: "Noble son, having gone to that Sahā world-system, you must not conceive a notion of inferiority toward it."
Furthermore, noble son, that world-system is indeed uneven,
consisting of earth, strewn with black mountains, and filled with cesspools; and that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has a short body.
And those bodhisattvas have short bodies;
whereas, noble son, your own physical form measures four million two hundred thousand yojanas,
and my own physical form, noble son, measures six million eight hundred thousand yojanas.
And you, noble son, are gracious, handsome, and beautiful,
endowed with the most excellent lotus-like complexion,
and possessed of a splendor exceeding hundreds of thousands of merits.
Therefore, son of good family, having gone to that Sahā world-system, do not conceive a notion of inferiority regarding the Tathāgata, the bodhisattvas, or that buddha-field.

When this had been said, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara spoke thus to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña: "Blessed One, I shall act exactly as the Tathāgata commands."

“Blessed One, by the empowerment of the Tathāgata, by the support of the Tathāgata’s power, by the Tathāgata’s sport, by the Tathāgata’s array, and by the Tathāgata’s exalted wisdom, I shall go to that Sahā world-system. Then, at that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, without even moving from that buddha-field and without rising from his seat, entered into such a samādhi.

As soon as the Bodhisattva Gadgadasvara had entered that samādhi, at that very moment, eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of lotuses appeared here in this Sahā world-system on Vulture Peak Mountain, in front of that Tathāgata’s Dharma-throne; they were seen with golden stalks, silver petals, and the color of the *kiṃśuka* flower.
Then Mañjuśrī, the Youthful, having seen that manifestation of the array of lotuses, addressed the Blessed One Śākyamuni,

the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Awakened One: "Blessed One, whose omen is this, by which these eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of lotuses with golden stalks and silver petals have appeared?"
"What are these colors, like those of the lotus and the *kiṃśuka* flower?

When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta: "Mañjuśrī, these come from the eastern direction, from the world-system called Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā, from that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña."

From the buddha-field of the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, surrounded and escorted by eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of bodhisattvas, is coming to this Sahā world-system to see me, to pay homage to me, to attend upon me,
and to hear this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what accumulation of merit has been performed by that son of good family, by which accumulation of merit—having been performed and accumulated—this distinction was obtained?
And in which samādhi, Blessed One, does that bodhisattva dwell?"
O Blessed One, may we hear of that samādhi, wherein, O Blessed One, we might practice;
and may we, O Blessed One, behold that bodhisattva mahāsattva.
What is the complexion of that bodhisattva, what is his form, and what is his characteristic?
"What is his appearance like? What is his conduct?
"Therefore, O Blessed One, may the Tathāgata perform such a sign by which, being thus impelled, that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva shall come to this Sahā world-system."

Then indeed, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, spoke thus to the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha who had entered parinirvāṇa: "May the Blessed One manifest such a sign by which..."
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara came to this Sahā world-system,
the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha who had entered parinirvāṇa,
at that very moment manifested such a sign for the sake of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara.

For the purpose of exhortation: "Come, noble son, to this Sahā world-system; Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta desires to see you. Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara [approached] that Blessed One, Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.
Having bowed his head at the feet of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and having circumambulated him three times,
he vanished from that world-system Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā, surrounded and escorted by those eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of bodhisattvas, and came to this Sahā world-system.
With the buddha-fields trembling,
lotuses raining down,
and hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of musical instruments being played;
With a face possessing eyes like blue lotuses and lotuses,
with a body of golden hue,
and with a physical form adorned by hundreds of thousands of merits;
Blazing with splendor, radiant with majesty, his limbs adorned with the primary marks, he possessed a body with the firm constitution of Nārāyaṇa.
Having ascended a peaked pavilion made of the seven precious gems, he approached, surrounded and escorted by a host of bodhisattvas, traveling through the air at a height of seven palm trees;
he drew near to this Sahā world-system and to Gṛdhrakūṭa, the king of mountains.
Having approached, he descended from that gabled hall, took a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold], and went toward where the Blessed One was.

Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him seven times, and offered that pearl necklace as an act of worship to the Blessed One. Having made the offering, he addressed the Blessed One: "O Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña..."

The Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, inquires after the Blessed One’s freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, ease of movement, well-being, strength, and dwelling in comfort.
And that Blessed One spoke thus: "Is it bearable for you, Blessed One?"
I hope you are maintaining yourself well; I hope your physical elements are in harmony; I hope those beings are of good character, easy to discipline, and easy to treat.
O Blessed One, may beings who are pure in body not be excessively prone to passion, nor excessively prone to hatred, nor excessively prone to delusion; may they not be envious, nor stingy.

May they not be ignorant of their mothers, may they not be ignorant of their fathers, may they not be non-monastic, may they not be non-brahminic, may they not hold wrong views, may they not have undisciplined minds, and may they not have unrestrained senses.
O Blessed One, have these beings had their Māras and adversaries defeated?
O Blessed One, has the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna—who has entered parinirvāṇa—come to this Sahā world-system to hear the Dharma within a stūpa made of the seven precious gems?
Standing in their midst,

that Blessed One questioned the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Greatly Enlightened One: "Is it well with that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Greatly Enlightened One Prabhūtaratna?"
"Is all well? Will the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, remain for long?
O Blessed One, may we also behold the relic-body of that Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"Therefore, may the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, graciously show us the relic-body of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna."
Then indeed, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, addressed the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat,
Samyaksaṃbuddha who had entered parinirvāṇa, saying: "Blessed One, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara [has come] to the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."

Desiring to see him who has entered final nirvāṇa, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna, then said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
It is indeed well that you have come here desiring to see the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
And [he came] to hear this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma and to see Mañjuśrī, the Youthful Prince.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrī said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what kind of roots of merit were previously planted by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, and in the presence of which Tathāgata?
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, [addressed] the Bodhisattva Padmaśrī...

He spoke thus to the Mahāsattva: "In the past, noble son, in a time long gone, in an aeon that was incalculable, more than incalculable, vast, immeasurable, and infinite, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Meghadundubhisvararāja."

There appeared in the world, in the eon named Priyadarśana, in the world-system Sarvarūpasaṃdarśanā, a Tathāgata, Arhat, perfectly enlightened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One,
named Meghadundubhisvararāja. Furthermore, O son of good family, of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat...
The bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara performed worship for the Samyaksaṃbuddha for twelve hundred thousand years by playing hundreds of thousands of musical instruments;
he also offered eighty-four thousand vessels made of the seven precious gems.
In that regard, noble son, it was under the teaching of the Tathāgata Meghadundubhisvararāja that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara attained such glory as this.

Now, noble son, you might perhaps have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation, thinking that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Gadgadasvara— who at that time and on that occasion performed the worship of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Meghadundubhisvararāja— was someone else.
"Have those eighty-four thousand vessels been given away?
Indeed, noble son, you should not view it in that way. For what reason?"
It was this very same noble son, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara,
who performed that worship for the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Meghadundubhisvararāja,
and offered those eighty-four thousand vessels.

In this way, noble son, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has attended upon many Buddhas; he has planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and has performed the preparatory practices for Buddhahood.

Furthermore, this bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has previously beheld Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges. Do you see this bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, Padmaśrī?
Padmaśrī said, "I see them, Blessed One; I see them, Sugata.
The Blessed One said, "Furthermore, Padmaśrī, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara indeed [manifests] in many forms for this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*."
He taught them;
that is to say: in some places in the form of Brahmā, in some places in the form of Rudra.
In some places in the form of Śakra, in some places in the form of Īśvara, and in some places in the form of a general;
In some places in the form of Vaiśravaṇa, in some places in the form of a universal monarch (cakravartin),
and in some places in the form of a local king (koṭṭarāja).
In some places in the form of a merchant,
in some places in the form of a householder, and in some places in the form of a member of the guild;
In some places, he taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* in the form of a brahmin;
in other places, in the form of a monk.
In some places in the form of a bhikṣuṇī, in some places in the form of an upāsaka,
in some places in the form of an upāsikā, and in some places in the form of a merchant’s wife.
In some places in the form of a householder’s wife, in some places in the form of a merchant’s wife, and in some places in the form of a young boy.
In some places, in the form of a young girl,
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* to sentient beings.
O son of good family, it was by such displays of forms that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* to sentient beings.
To some, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* in the form of a yakṣa;
to some, in the form of a deva;
and to some, in the form of a garuḍa.

To some he taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* in the form of a *kinnara*, and to others in the form of a *mahoraga*; in this way, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* to sentient beings, even those born in the hells, the animal realm, the world of Yama, or in other unfavorable states, acting as their savior.
It was so;

even for those beings who had entered the midst of the inner apartments, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, having manifested in the form of a woman, taught this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma to those beings.

In this Sahā world-system, he taught the Dharma to sentient beings. Indeed, Padmaśrī, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara is a protector of the sentient beings born in the Sahā world-system. And in that very Sahā world-system, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara [taught] this Dharma-discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* to sentient beings through such various forms and signs.
He teaches the Dharma;
yet there is no decline in the supernatural powers of this true person, nor is there any decline in his wisdom.
By means of such illuminations of knowledge, noble son, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara is known in this Sahā world-system.
And in other world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a bodhisattva to those beings who are to be disciplined by a bodhisattva;
he teaches the Dharma in the form of a śrāvaka to those beings who are to be disciplined by a śrāvaka.
To those beings who are to be disciplined by a Pratyekabuddha, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a Pratyekabuddha;
to those beings who are to be disciplined by a Tathāgata, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a Tathāgata;
and so on, up to showing the Tathāgata-realm to those beings who are to be disciplined by the Tathāgata-realm.
He displays himself as having entered final nirvana for as long as there are beings to be guided by that means until their own final nirvana.
Thus, Padmaśrī, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has indeed attained the empowerment of the power of gnosis.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrī said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has planted roots of merit.
Blessed One, what is this samādhi in which the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara abides, by means of which he has disciplined so many sentient beings?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrī: "Noble son, this is the samādhi called 'Manifestation of All Forms.
While established in this samādhi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara has performed such immeasurable benefit for sentient beings."

Furthermore, while this "Chapter on Gadgadasvara" was being taught, all those eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of kotis of bodhisattvas who had come to this Sahā world-system together with the bodhisattva mahāsattva Gadgadasvara attained the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms."
And in this Sahā world-system,
there were incalculable numbers of bodhisattva mahāsattvas who had attained the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara, having performed a vast and extensive worship of the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and of the reliquary stupa of the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, ascended once again into the gabled pavilion made of the seven precious gems.

Surrounded and escorted by those eighty-four hundred thousand *koṭī-nayuta* bodhisattvas, he returned once more to his own buddha-field, accompanied by trembling lands, raining lotuses, and the sounding of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of musical instruments.

Having approached the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, he said this to him: "Blessed One, I have accomplished the welfare of sentient beings in the Sahā world-system;
and I have seen and paid homage to the relic stupa of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna."
And that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, was seen and saluted;
and that Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta was seen; and that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, who has attained the impetus of the power of vigor, was seen.
And that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Pradānaśūra was seen;
and all those eighty-four hundred thousand nayutas of koṭis of Bodhisattvas attained the samādhi called "Manifestation of All Forms."

Furthermore, while this chapter on the coming and going of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gadgadasvara was being spoken, forty-two thousand bodhisattvas attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*),
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrī attained the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* samādhi.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, titled "Gadgadasvara," in the Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
(Vaidya 250) Saddhp_24: The Chapter on the Universal Gate (Samantamukha).
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder,

placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "For what reason, Blessed One, is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara called 'Avalokiteśvara'?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati: "In this world, noble son, however many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings there may be who experience various sufferings,
if they should hear the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
they shall all be completely liberated from that mass of suffering."
And, noble son, those beings who hold the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
if they should fall into a great mass of fire,
they shall all be liberated from that great mass of fire by the power of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, noble son, if beings who are being swept away by rivers should cry out to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
all those rivers will provide a firm footing for those beings.
Furthermore, noble son, if hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of beings have boarded ships in the midst of the ocean...

Suppose that ship, laden with treasures of gold, fine gold, jewels, pearls, diamonds, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, corals, emeralds, musāragalva, red pearls, and so forth, were cast by a black wind onto the island of the rākṣasīs;
and suppose there were only a single sentient being remaining on it who would cry out for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
They shall all be completely liberated from that island of rākṣasīs.
For this reason, noble son, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara is known as "Avalokiteśvara."

If, noble son, someone condemned to death should cry out to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the weapons of those executioners would shatter into pieces. Furthermore, noble son, even if this triple-thousand great-thousand world system were filled with yakṣas and rākṣasas, [it would be no obstacle].
By grasping the name of the Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, they would be unable even to look upon those with malicious intent.
Furthermore, noble son, if any being whatsoever were bound in wooden or iron stocks and shackles, whether guilty or innocent, [they would be released].
By merely grasping the name of that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, those bonds of shackles and fetters quickly yield an opening.
Such, noble son, is the power of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
If, noble son, this triple-thousand great-thousand world system were filled with rogues, enemies, and thieves bearing weapons in their hands,

and a certain caravan leader were traveling through it having taken a great caravan carrying abundant, priceless jewels; and as they traveled, they were to see those thieves, rogues, and enemies with weapons in their hands.
And having seen this, they would become afraid and terrified, perceiving themselves to be without refuge.
Then that caravan leader would say to that caravan: "Do not fear, sons of good family; do not fear."

"Call out with one voice to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Giver of Fearlessness! Then you shall be swiftly delivered from this danger of robbers and this danger of enemies. Thereupon, that entire caravan called out to Avalokiteśvara with one voice: "Homage, homage to that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Giver of Fearlessness!"
By the mere utterance of his name, that caravan would be delivered from all fears.
Such, O son of good family, is the power of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Noble son, those beings who are characterized by passion,
having paid homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, become free from passion. Those beings who are characterized by hatred...
Having paid homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, those who are prone to hatred become free from hatred;
those beings who are prone to delusion,
having paid homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, become free from delusion.
In this way, noble son, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara possesses such great supernatural power.
And if, noble son, a woman desiring a son pays homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, she gives birth to a son who is handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold;
he is endowed with the marks of a son, beloved by many people, charming, and one who has planted roots of merit.

For one who rejoices in a daughter, a daughter is born to him— one who is beautiful, pleasing, and lovely to behold, endowed with the highest excellence of complexion and form; a daughter possessed of auspicious marks, beloved and charming to many people,
and one who has planted roots of merit.
Such, noble son, is the power of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
And, noble son, for those who shall pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and who shall hold his name in mind,
their fruit shall be unfailing.
And, noble son, whoever shall pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and retain his name,
and whoever shall pay homage to as many Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as there are grains of sand in sixty-two Ganges rivers— [the merit of the former would be greater].
And one should also retain their names. Now,

suppose someone were to make offerings to those very same Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, while they are staying, remaining, and living, providing them with robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick—
what do you think, noble son, how much of a formation of merit would that noble son or noble daughter produce on that account?
When this had been said, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati said this to the Blessed One: "Much, Blessed One;
much, Sugata, would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate as a result of that great accumulation of merit.
The Blessed One said: "And as for the accumulation of merit from a son of good family who has performed such an act of honor toward those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones—"

And whoever should offer even a single prostration to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and bear his name in mind, the accumulation of merit from these two would be equal, neither more nor less.
And whoever should pay honor to those sixty-two Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, and bear their names in mind— [the merit of these two would be equal].
And whoever should pay homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and uphold his name—
these two accumulations of merit would not be easy to exhaust even in hundreds of thousands of nayutas of kotis of eons.
Thus, noble son, immeasurable is the merit from upholding the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, how does the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teach the Dharma to sentient beings in this Sahā world-system?
And what is the scope of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara’s skill in means?"

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the bodhisattva mahāsattva Akṣayamati: "Noble son, there are world-systems in which the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma to sentient beings in the form of a Buddha.
There are world-systems," [he continued].

In some places, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma to sentient beings in the form of a bodhisattva; for some, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma to sentient beings in the form of a pratyekabuddha;
and for others, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma to sentient beings in the form of a śrāvaka.
To some, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma to sentient beings in the form of Brahmā;
to some, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma in the form of Śakra;
and to some, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma to sentient beings in the form of a Gandharva.
To some, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara teaches the Dharma in the form of a gandharva;
to those beings who are to be disciplined by a yakṣa, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a yakṣa;
and to those beings who are to be disciplined by Īśvara, he [teaches it] in the form of Īśvara.
To those beings who are to be disciplined by Maheśvara, he teaches the Dharma in the form of Maheśvara;
to those beings who are to be disciplined by a universal monarch (cakravartin), he teaches the Dharma in the form of a universal monarch;
to those beings who are to be disciplined by a piśāca, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a piśāca.
To those beings who are to be converted by Vaiśravaṇa, he teaches the Dharma in the form of Vaiśravaṇa;
to those beings who are to be converted by a general, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a general;
to those beings who are to be converted by a brahmin, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a brahmin.
To those beings who are to be converted by Vajrapāṇi, he teaches the Dharma in the form of Vajrapāṇi.
Thus, noble son, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara is endowed with such inconceivable qualities.
Therefore, noble son, you should worship the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
Noble son, this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara grants fearlessness to frightened beings;
for this reason, he is known as "Giver of Fearlessness" here in this Sahā world-system.
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, we shall give a gift of Dharma, a covering of Dharma, to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
The Blessed One said: "Noble son, do now as you deem the time right."

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati, having taken from his own neck a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold], presented it as a religious gift to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Accept this religious gift from me, O Noble Being."
He did not accept it.
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Noble son, out of compassion for us, please accept this pearl necklace.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara [accepted it] from the presence of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣayamati.

Out of compassion for the bodhisattva mahāsattva Akṣayamati, and out of compassion for those four assemblies and for the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, he accepted that pearl necklace. Having accepted it, he divided it into two portions.

Having divided it into two portions, he gave one portion to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, and he presented the second portion to the stupa of jewels of the Blessed One Prabhūtaratna, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha.
It is with such miraculous power, noble son, that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara wanders throughout this Sahā world-system.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Citradhvaja, you of inexhaustible intelligence, have asked about this matter for a specific reason."
O Son of the Conqueror, for what reason is he called Avalokiteśvara?
Then, having looked toward the ten directions, Citradhvaja, whose resolve was an inexhaustible ocean, spoke thus: "Listen to the conduct of Avalokiteśvara."
Listen to me as I describe, even in part, how my vow was purified over many hundreds of millions of inconceivable eons by thousands of millions of Buddhas.
Hearing it, as well as seeing it, and likewise successive recollection of it,
becomes unfailing for living beings here, destroying all suffering and the sorrow of existence.
If one with a corrupt mind should throw [a person] into a pit of fire for the purpose of killing him,
the fire is extinguished as if sprinkled with water when he calls Avalokiteśvara to mind.
Even if one should fall into the perilous ocean, the abode of nāgas, makaras, asuras, and spirits,
one who recollects Avalokiteśvara will never sink in the king of waters.
Even if one with a corrupted mind were to hurl [a person] from the summit of Mount Meru for the purpose of killing them,
if they remember Avalokiteśvara, they will remain in the sky like the sun.
Even if a mountain made of diamond were to fall upon one's head for the purpose of crushing it,
when one recollects Avalokiteśvara, they will not be able to harm even a single pore of one's skin.
Even if one is surrounded by hosts of enemies with weapons in their hands and murderous intent,
if they remember Avalokiteśvara, at that very moment their minds will become filled with loving-kindness.
Even if one has arrived at the place of execution and is under the power of the executioners,
if they remember Avalokiteśvara, then the weapons shall fall into pieces.
If one here is bound with bonds of wooden or iron shackles and fetters,
upon remembering Avalokiteśvara, those bonds will quickly fall apart.
Spells, powers, sciences, medicinal herbs, spirits, and vetālas that destroy the body—
upon remembering Avalokiteśvara, they depart back to wherever they originated.
Even if one is surrounded by those who steal vitality— nāgas, yakṣas, gods, bhūtas, and rākṣasas—
they are not able to harm even a single pore of one who remembers Avalokiteśvara.
Even if one is surrounded by fierce beasts with sharp fangs and claws that inspire great terror,
if they call Avalokiteśvara to mind, they quickly flee in all directions to the ends of the earth.
Even if one is surrounded by those whose gaze is poisonous, who are as fierce and terrible as the flames of a blazing fire,
they will quickly become free of poison upon remembering Avalokiteśvara.
Deep thunder, lightning, clouds, vajra-thunderbolts, and torrents of water—
all these are instantly and immediately pacified at that very moment for one who recollects Avalokiteśvara. (Saddhp 24.16)

Having beheld beings afflicted by hundreds of manifold sufferings and tormented by great misery, he who possesses the power of pure knowledge looked upon them; therefore, he is the savior of the world including the gods.
Having reached the perfection of the power of supernatural faculties, possessing vast wisdom and trained in skillful means,
he is seen everywhere throughout the world in all directions and in all realms without exception.
And those fears of the unfavorable states and miserable rebirths— of hell, the animal realm, and the domain of Yama—
as well as the afflictions of birth, old age, and sickness, are gradually pacified for living beings.
Then Akṣamati, with a heart thrilled and joyful, spoke these verses:
"O you of auspicious eyes, of eyes of loving-kindness, of eyes distinguished by wisdom and knowledge;
O you of compassionate eyes, of pure eyes, lovely, fair-faced, and of beautiful eyes! (Saddhp 24.20)
With stainless, pure, and immaculate radiance, with the light of the sun of knowledge that dispels darkness,
and with a brilliance that has extinguished the flames of the winds, you shine forth, scorching the world.

Thundering with compassion, excellent qualities, and loving-kindness, you are a great cloud whose mind is filled with auspicious virtues and friendliness; you extinguish the fire of the afflictions of living beings and rain down the nectar of the supreme Dharma.
In times of strife, dispute, and conflict, when men have fallen into the great terror of battle,
by remembering Avalokiteśvara, the hosts of evil enemies shall be pacified. (Saddhp 24.23)
With a voice like a cloud, a drum, the roar of the ocean, and the exquisite sound of Brahmā;
having reached the perfection of the entire range of sounds—Avalokiteśvara is to be remembered.
Remember, remember him with longing—the Pure Being Avalokiteśvara!
In death, in calamity, and in distress, he becomes a protector, a refuge, and a final resort.
Having reached the perfection of all virtues, with eyes of compassion and loving-kindness toward all beings,
Avalokiteśvara is a source of merit, an ocean of great qualities, and worthy of veneration.
I bow down to Avalokiteśvara, that compassionate one who will become a Buddha in a future age, the destroyer of all suffering, fear, and sorrow.
Lokeśvara, the leader of kings, a monk who is a mine of Dharma and honored by the world,
having practiced for many hundreds of eons, attained stainless, unsurpassed awakening.
Standing to the right and left, they likewise fan the Leader Amitābha;
through the samādhi of the illusory-like nature, they go to all fields and worship the Jinas.
In the western direction is the world-system Sukhāvatī, free from dust and a source of happiness,
where this leader Amitābha, the charioteer of beings, currently resides.
There is no possibility of women there, nor is there any sexual intercourse whatsoever;
those sons of the Jina are born spontaneously, seated within the calyxes of lotuses, stainless.
And that very Leader Amitābha, seated upon a lion throne within the stainless and delightful Padmagarbha world-system, shines forth like a sal tree in full bloom.
So too is that Leader of the World, to whom there is no equal in the three realms of existence;
by whatever merit I have accumulated through praising him, may I quickly become like you, O Supreme among Men.
Thus [it is said].
Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Dharaṇīdhara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder,

placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows: "Blessed One, those sentient beings will not be endowed with inferior roots of merit."
Those who shall hear this chapter of the Dharma-discourse of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—

this exposition of the miraculous transformations of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, titled "The Chapter on the Universal Gate," which is the miraculous display of the transformations of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

Furthermore, while this chapter on the Universal Gate was being taught by the Blessed One, the minds of eighty-four thousand beings in that assembly were set upon the peerless, incomparable, and unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of the Transformations of Avalokiteśvara," in the Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
(Vaidya 258) Chapter 25: The Former Deeds of King Śubhavyūha.
Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of bodhisattvas: "In the past, sons of good family, in a time long gone, more than incalculable eons ago, there was a time..."
At that time, at that very moment, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña—

one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One— in the eon called Priyadarśana, within the world-system Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā.
Furthermore, noble sons, during the teaching of that Tathāgata Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, there was a king named Śubhavyūha.
Furthermore, noble sons, that King Śubhavyūha had a wife named Vimaladattā.
Furthermore, noble sons, that King Śubhavyūha had two sons: one named Vimalagarbha, and...
The second was named Vimalanetra;
and those two boys were both possessed of growth, endowed with wisdom, merit, and knowledge, and were devoted to the conduct of a bodhisattva.
That is to say: they were devoted to the perfection of generosity,

the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditation, the perfection of wisdom, the perfection of skillful means, to loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, up to and including the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.
They had reached the further shore in all things;
they had reached the further shore of the stainless samādhi,
and they had reached the further shore of the samādhi of the Sun-like King of Constellations.
They had reached the further shore of the concentration called Vimalanirbhāsa; they had reached the further shore of the concentration called Vimalabhāsa;
they had reached the further shore of the concentration called Alaṃkāraśubha.
They both reached the further shore of the samādhi called Mahātejogarbha.
And at that time, on that occasion, the Blessed One taught this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* out of compassion for those beings and out of compassion for King Śubhavyūha.
Then, noble sons, the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra approached their own mother, their progenitress;
having approached her, they joined their ten fingers in reverent salutation and said this to their mother: "Come, Mother, we shall go to him."
To the presence of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña,
in order to see and pay homage to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.
for the purpose of attending upon him.
And why is that?
Because, O Mother, he is that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.
"The Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, is extensively proclaiming the Dharma discourse named the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* before the world including the devas;
we shall go to hear it."

When this had been said, noble sons, the queen Vimaladattā spoke thus to the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra: "Noble sons, this father of yours, King Śubhavyūha, has placed his faith in the brahmins;
therefore, you will not be permitted to go to see that Tathāgata."

Then, noble sons, the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra, joining their ten fingers in reverent salutation, said this to their own mother, their progenitress: "Were we born into this family of false views? Are we not rather the sons of the King of Dharma?"

Then, noble sons, Queen Vimaladattā said this to those two boys: "Excellent, excellent, noble sons! Out of compassion for your father, King Śubhavyūha, display some kind of miraculous feat so that he might indeed place his faith in you."
And with a serene mind, may he grant us permission to approach that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.

Then, noble sons, at that moment the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra, out of compassion for their father King Śubhavyūha, rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees and, authorized by the Buddha, performed twin miracles.
They performed miracles;
having gone right there into the air, they prepared their beds,
and they walked back and forth right there in the air.
Right there in the sky, they shook off dust;
right there in the sky, they emitted streams of water from their lower bodies and caused masses of fire to blaze forth from their upper bodies.
From their upper bodies they emitted streams of water, and from their lower bodies they caused masses of fire to blaze forth;
becoming large in that very space, they then became small.
Having become small, they become large;
they vanish in that very same space and emerge from the earth.
Emerging from the earth, they emerged into the sky.
Indeed, noble sons, by means of such miraculous displays of supernatural power (*ṛddhiprātihārya*), those two boys converted their father, King Śubhavyūha.
