Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha, having witnessed that miraculous display of supernatural power by the two boys, [was moved].

At that time, being satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and cheer, he joined his ten fingers in reverent salutation and said this to those two boys: "Noble sons, who is your teacher, and whose disciples are you?"
Then, noble sons, those two boys said this to King Śubhavyūha:

"Great King, there is that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña; he dwells, remains, and sustains himself, seated upon the Dharma-throne at the foot of the jewel-adorned Bodhi tree."
In the presence of the world with its gods, he extensively proclaims the Dharma discourse named *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
That Blessed One is our Teacher; we two, O Great King, are his disciples.
Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha said to those two boys: "Noble sons, let us see that teacher of yours;
we shall go into the presence of that Blessed One."
Then, noble sons, those two boys descended from the sky and approached their own mother, their progenitor.

Having approached, they joined their ten fingers in reverent salutation and said this to their mother, their progenitor: "Mother, our father has been trained by us in unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
We have performed for our father the duty of a teacher."
Therefore, you ought to relinquish it now;
we two shall go forth into homelessness in the presence of that Blessed One.

Then, noble sons, at that time the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra addressed their mother, their own progenitor, with these two verses: "Grant us your permission, Mother, for the homeless life of renunciation;
we two shall indeed go forth, for a Tathāgata is difficult to encounter."
Just as the udumbara flower is extremely rare to find, so too is a Jina;
having renounced the world, we shall go forth into homelessness, for the perfection of the opportune moment is difficult to obtain.
Vimaladattā, the king’s wife, said:
“I release you both today; go forth, my dear children!
We too shall go forth into the religious life, for a Tathāgata is indeed difficult to encounter.”
Thus [it is said].
Then, noble sons, having spoken these two verses, those two boys said this to their parents: "Excellent, mother and father, come!
Let us all go together into the presence of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña."
We shall go to that Blessed One to see him, to pay homage to him, to attend upon him, and to hear the Dharma.
For what reason?
Because, mother and father, the appearance of a Buddha is indeed rare.

"O Mother, the appearance of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, is as difficult to encounter as the blooming of the udumbara flower, or like a turtle thrusting its neck through the hole of a yoke floating upon the great ocean.
Therefore, O Mother and Father, we have been sustained by supreme merit to have been born into such a teaching."
Therefore, mother and father, please grant us permission;
we two shall go.
We will go forth into the religious life in the presence of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.
For it is rare, O mother and father, to behold the Tathāgatas;
for rare indeed is this time,
and such is the King of Dharma.
Such a perfection of the opportune moment is extremely difficult to obtain.
Furthermore, noble sons, at that time eighty-four thousand women from the harem of King Śubhavyūha became vessels for this Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma;
and the boy Vimalanetra had already practiced in this Dharma discourse.

And the boy Vimalagarbha had practiced for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons in the samādhi called "Eliminating the Evil of All Sentient Beings," thinking, "How might all sentient beings eliminate all evil?

Furthermore, their mother, the queen Vimaladattā, understood the assemblies of all Buddhas and the secret points of all the Buddha-dharmas. Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha was disciplined by those two boys in the teaching of the Tathāgata.
He caused his entire retinue of kinsmen to descend [to the Dharma] and brought them to maturity;
and so too did Queen Vimaladattā, together with her entire retinue of kinsmen, and those two sons of King Śubhavyūha.

The two sons, together with forty-two thousand living beings, along with their harem and their ministers— all joined together as one— proceeded toward where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña was staying.
Approaching him,
they bowed their heads at the feet of that Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood to one side.

Then, noble sons, that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, perceiving that King Śubhavyūha had approached together with his retinue, instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the Dharma.
Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha— having been well and thoroughly instructed, exhorted, inspired, and gladdened by that Blessed One with a discourse on the Dharma—

at that moment became satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; he bound the turban upon his younger brother, established him in the kingdom, and together with his sons, kinsmen, and retinue,
as well as Queen Vimaladattā and her entire company of women, [departed].
And those two boys, together with those forty-two thousand living beings—

all of them united and assembled— out of faith went forth from the home to the homeless life in the teaching of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña.

Having gone forth into homelessness, King Śubhavyūha, together with his retinue, dwelt diligently for eighty-four thousand years, contemplating, cultivating, and mastering this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
Then, noble sons, at the conclusion of those eighty-four thousand years, that King Śubhavyūha attained the samādhi called "The Array of the Ornament of All Virtues."
And as soon as he had attained this samādhi, he immediately rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees.

Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha, standing in the sky, addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña: "Blessed One, these two sons of mine have become my teachers;
for by means of their miraculous power, I was turned away from that great mass of false views."
He has been established in the teaching of the Tathāgata,
brought to maturity, introduced [to it],
and exhorted to behold the Tathāgata.
"Blessed One, those two boys are my spiritual friends who have been born in my house in the form of sons, namely for the purpose of causing me to remember my former roots of merit."
When this had been said, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, spoke thus to King Śubhavyūha:
"So it is, Great King; so it is, just as you say."

For those sons of good family and daughters of good family, O Great King, who have planted roots of merit, spiritual friends are easily found throughout all states of existence, destinies, deaths, and rebirths; they appear to perform the work of a Teacher,
acting as instructors, introducers, and maturers for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
"O Great King, this is a sublime matter, namely, the taking hold of a spiritual friend who leads one to behold the Tathāgata.
Do you see these two boys, O Great King?
He replied, "I see them, Blessed One."
"I see them, Sugata.

The Blessed One said: "Furthermore, Great King, these two sons of good family will perform worship in the presence of as many Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas as there are grains of sand in sixty-five Ganges rivers;
and out of compassion for sentient beings, they will uphold this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma."
And for the sake of generating vigor in beings with wrong views so that they may attain right view.
Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha descended from the expanse of the sky, joined his ten fingers in reverent salutation,
and addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, saying: "It would be well, Blessed One!"
May the Tathāgata explain: endowed with what kind of knowledge is the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, by which the uṣṇīṣa shines upon his crown,
the Blessed One possesses stainless eyes,
and between his eyebrows the ūrṇā shines with a radiance as white as the moon or a conch shell?
And that row of teeth, even and closely set, shines within his mouth;
the Blessed One has lips like the *bimba* fruit, beautiful eyes, and is the Sugata.

Then, noble sons, King Śubhavyūha, having praised that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña with these qualities and with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of other virtues, [proceeded to...]

Having praised the Blessed One, at that time he addressed the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, saying: "It is marvelous, Blessed One, how great is the purpose of this teaching of the Tathāgata; and inconceivable are the qualities endowed with which is the Dharma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata."
Since the training of the Tathāgata is so well-proclaimed,
from this day forward, O Blessed One, we shall no longer be under the sway of the mind,
nor shall we again be under the sway of wrong views.
We shall no longer be under the sway of anger,
nor shall we again be under the sway of the arising of evil thoughts.
Blessed One, being endowed with such a multitude of unwholesome qualities, I did not wish to approach the presence of the Blessed One.
Having bowed his head at the feet of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrajasaṃkusumitābhijña, he remained suspended in mid-air.
Then, indeed, King Śubhavyūha and his queen Vimaladattā cast a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [gold pieces] into the air above the Blessed One.
As soon as that pearl necklace was cast, it became a gabled pavilion (*kūṭāgāra*) resting upon the head of the Blessed One—quadrangular, with four pillars, symmetrical, and well-proportioned.
And within that gabled pavilion, a couch appeared, spread with many hundreds of thousands of fine cloths.
And upon that couch, the form of the Tathāgata was seen sitting cross-legged.
Then, this thought occurred to King Śubhavyūha: "Great is the majesty of this Buddha-knowledge;
the Tathāgata is endowed with inconceivable qualities."
For here indeed this form of the Tathāgata is seen situated within the peaked roof palace, gracious, beautiful to behold, and endowed with the most excellent lotus-like complexion.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña, addressed the four assemblies: "Monks, do you see King Śubhavyūha standing in the expanse of the sky, roaring the lion's roar?"
They said, "We see him, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said, "Monks, this King Śubhavyūha shall indeed enter the state of a monk within my teaching and become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Śālendrarāja in the world;

he will be endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One, in the world-system Vistīrṇavatī."
That eon shall be named Abhyudgatarāja.
Furthermore, monks, that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śālendrarāja will have an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas and an immeasurable assembly of śrāvakas.
That world-system Vistīrṇavatī will be level like the palm of a hand and consist of vaidūrya.
In this way, that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha will be inconceivable.
Furthermore, noble sons, you might have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation, thinking: "Was that King named Śubhavyūha at that time and on that occasion someone else?"
Furthermore, sons of good family, you should not view it in this way.
And why is that?
This very Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrī was, at that time and on that occasion, the king named Śubhavyūha.
"Furthermore, noble sons, you might perhaps have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation, thinking that at that time and on that occasion, the king's wife named Vimaladattā was someone else.
But, noble sons, you must certainly not view it in this way."
For what reason?
This very Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitadhvajārāja was, at that time and on that occasion, the queen of the king named Vimaladattā;
he had accepted the role of being the wife of King Śubhavyūha out of compassion for that king and for those sentient beings.
Furthermore, sons of good family, you might perhaps have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation, thinking that those two boys at that time and on that occasion were someone else.
But, sons of good family, you must certainly not view it in this way.
And why is that?
Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata were, at that time and on that occasion, the two sons of King Śubhavyūha.
Thus, noble sons, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata are endowed with such inconceivable qualities;
they have planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas.
Both of these two virtuous persons are endowed with inconceivable qualities;
and all those who shall uphold the names of these two virtuous persons will become worthy of homage by the world together with its devas.
Furthermore, while this chapter on the former connection was being spoken, the dust-free and stainless Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena was purified in eighty-four thousand living beings.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled "The Former Deeds of King Śubhavyūha," in the Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.
(Vaidya 264) Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra, Chapter 26: Encouragement by Samantabhadra.
Then, indeed, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, together with incalculable Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas from the eastern direction, [arrived].
Accompanied, surrounded, and honored by [the assembly], amidst trembling lands, raining lotuses, and the sounding of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of musical instruments,

he proceeded with the great majesty of a bodhisattva, the great miraculous display of a bodhisattva, the great supernatural power of a bodhisattva, the great nobility of a bodhisattva, the great meditative composure of a bodhisattva, and blazing with the great splendor of a bodhisattva.

Surrounded by a great multitude of those belonging to the Bodhisattva vehicle, by a great display of the miraculous powers of a Bodhisattva, and by a vast assembly of gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
Honored in this way by inconceivable miraculous displays of supernatural power, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra arrived at this world-system;
he approached the king of mountains, Gṛdhrakūṭa, and went to where the Blessed One was.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him seven times, and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Blessed One, I have come here from the buddha-field of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnatejobhyudgatarāja.
Blessed One, it is because this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* is being taught here in this Sahā world-system."
I have come into the presence of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, in order to hear it.

And, Blessed One, these hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas have also come to hear this Dharma discourse, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*. Therefore, it would be well if the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, would teach this Dharma discourse, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, in detail to these bodhisattva mahāsattvas.

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra: "Noble son, these Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas are indeed possessors of realized knowledge (*uddhaṭitajña*).
Nevertheless, this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*—that is to say, the undifferentiated suchness (*asaṃbhinnatathatā*)—is [beyond them].
Those Bodhisattvas said: "So it is, Blessed One."
"So be it, Sugata. Then, indeed,

for the sake of establishing those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who had assembled in that assembly in the Dharma-discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*, the Blessed One once again [addressed] Samantabhadra.

He said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: "Noble son, when a woman is endowed with four qualities, this Dharma discourse of the White Lotus of the Good Dharma will come into her hands. What are the four?"
Namely: he will be sustained by the blessed Buddhas; he will have planted roots of merit;
and yet he will remain situated within the mass of those destined for hell.
For the sake of protecting all sentient beings, she will resolve her mind upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Noble son, this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* shall come into the hands of a woman who is endowed with these four qualities.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One,
in the future time, in the final period, during the last five hundred years, I shall provide protection for those monks who uphold such sūtras as these."
I shall perform a rite for well-being; I shall perform a rite for the avoidance of punishment; I shall perform a rite for the neutralization of poison.
In such a way that no one seeking an entry-point or searching for an entry-point against those Dharma-preachers shall find an opportunity;
neither Māra the Evil One, nor Māra’s sons, nor the gods of Māra’s host, nor Māra’s daughters, nor Māra’s retinue shall find an opportunity, until he is no longer possessed by the obsession of Māra.

Neither gods, nor yakṣas, nor pretas, nor pūtanas, nor kṛtyās, nor vetālas shall find an opportunity, seek an opportunity, or gain an opportunity against that Dharma-preacher who looks for and seeks an opening.
Blessed One, I shall constantly, continuously, and at all times provide protection for that Dharma-preacher.
And whenever that Dharma-preacher, devoted to the application of reflection upon this Dharma-discourse, shall be engaged in walking meditation, [I shall protect him].

Then, Blessed One, having mounted the white six-tusked king of elephants, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, I shall approach the walking-pavilion of that Dharma-preacher for the sake of protecting this Dharma-discourse.

Furthermore, when that Dharma-preacher— while devoted to the application of thought regarding this Dharma-discourse— should happen to lose even a single word or syllable from this Dharma-discourse, [I shall restore it].
Then, having mounted that king of elephants, Śvetasaddanta, and having presented myself before that Dharma-preacher, I shall recite this Dharma-discourse in its entirety for him.

And that Dharma-preacher, seeing my physical form and hearing this Dharma-discourse in its entirety from me, will become satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; he will, to an even greater degree, apply himself with vigor toward this Dharma-discourse.

With a joyful heart, delighted and filled with gladness and happiness, he will apply himself with even greater vigor to this Dharma discourse; and upon merely seeing me, he will attain meditative concentration and will also attain the dhāraṇī named Dhāraṇyāvartā.
He will obtain the dhāraṇī named *Koṭīśatasahasrāvartā*,
and he will obtain the dhāraṇī named *Sarvarutakauśalyāvartā*.

And those, Blessed One, who in the future time, in the future period, during the final five hundred years— whether they be monks or nuns, or laymen or laywomen— who are thus upholders of this sūtra, thus writers of this sūtra, thus seekers of this sūtra, and thus reciters of this sūtra, regarding this dharma-discourse in that future time, in that future period, during the final five hundred years;
For three weeks, or twenty-one days, they shall remain intent and engaged while walking up and down.
To them, I will manifest my own body as Sarvasattvapriyadarśana.
Mounted upon that very same white elephant king with six tusks, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, I will come to the walking path of those Dharma-preachers on the twenty-first day.
And having arrived, I shall gladden those Dharma-preachers, incite them, inspire them, and fill them with joy;
and I shall grant them a dhāraṇī,
so that those Dharma-preachers will not be overcome by anyone.
Neither humans nor non-humans shall find an opportunity to harm them,
nor shall women lead them astray;
and I shall provide them with protection.
I shall perform a rite for well-being; I shall perform a rite to avoid punishment; I shall perform a rite to neutralize poison.
"Blessed One, we shall grant these *dhāraṇī* phrases to those Dharma-preachers.
Blessed One, those *dhāraṇī* phrases are as follows:
*adaṇḍe*, *daṇḍapati*, *daṇḍāvartani*, *daṇḍakuśale*, *daṇḍasudhāri*, *sudhārapati*, *buddhapaśyane*."

O you who hold all, O you who turn back, O you who transform, O you who examine the Saṅgha, O you who destroy the Saṅgha, O you who examine the Dharma, O you who have entered into skill in the sounds of all beings, O you who sport like a lion, O follower, O path-maker, O Vartāli, svāhā!
"Blessed One, it should be known that when these dhāraṇī phrases come within the range of the sense of hearing of any bodhisattva mahāsattva,
this is the empowerment of the bodhisattva mahāsattva Samantabhadra."

And, Blessed One, as this Dharma-discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* circulates in this Jambudvīpa, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas into whose hands it shall come, Blessed One, those Dharma-preachers should understand this: "It is through the power of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Samantabhadra that this Dharma-discourse has come into our hands; it is through the majesty of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Samantabhadra."
Blessed One, those beings will become recipients of the conduct of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra;
moreover, those beings will have planted roots of merit under many Buddhas.
And those beings, Blessed One, who shall write down and uphold this sutra will have their heads stroked by the hand of the Tathāgata;
they, Blessed One, will have done what is pleasing to me.

Those who shall write down this sūtra, and those who shall understand its meaning— having written it down, O Blessed One, they will, upon passing away from here, be reborn in the company of the Trāyastriṃśa gods.
And as soon as they are born, eighty-four thousand apsarases will approach them;
with crowns as large as drums, those sons of gods will stand in the midst of those apsarases.
Such, noble son, is the mass of merit from writing down this Dharma-discourse.
How much more so for those who shall expound it, recite it, contemplate it, and attend to it in their minds!
Therefore, sons of good family, this Dharma-discourse of the White Lotus of the True Dharma should be written down with reverence, having focused the mind upon it at all times.
And whoever shall write it with undistracted mental attention, to him a thousand Buddhas will extend their hands,
and at the time of death, a thousand Buddhas will appear before his very eyes.
Nor will he go to a state of woe or a fallen rebirth;
having passed away from here, he will be reborn in the company of the Tuṣita gods,
where that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya resides.
Endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man, surrounded by a multitude of Bodhisattvas, and honored by hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of apsarases, he teaches the Dharma.

Therefore, sons of good family, this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* should be respectfully written down by a wise son of good family or daughter of good family; it should be respectfully recited, and it should be respectfully studied.
It should be attended to with reverence.
Sons of good family, by writing down this Dharma-discourse, teaching it, reciting it, cultivating it, and attending to it, such immeasurable qualities will arise.
Therefore, O Blessed One, that wise son of good family or daughter of good family should uphold this Dharma-discourse, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
Such shall be the extent of their qualities and benefits.
Therefore, O Blessed One, I too shall empower this Dharma discourse,
so that by my empowerment, O Blessed One, this Dharma discourse will circulate in this Jambudvīpa.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra: "Excellent, excellent, Samantabhadra!

For it is indeed so that you have set out for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great mass of beings."
Thus you are endowed with inconceivable qualities, through a resolute intention embraced by great compassion and by the production of the thought of awakening embraced by the inconceivable,
since you yourself provide empowerment for those Dharma-preachers.
Whosoever, sons of good family, shall uphold the name of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, it should be known by them that they have seen the Tathāgata Śākyamuni;
and this Dharma discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* has been heard by them from the presence of that Blessed One, Śākyamuni.
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni will be honored by them,
and they will offer their acclaim to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni as he teaches the Dharma.
They will rejoice in this Dharma-discourse, and the Tathāgata Śākyamuni will place his hand upon the heads of those beings.
And the Blessed One Śākyamuni will be covered by those robes;
Samantabhadra, those sons of good family or daughters of good family should be known as upholders of the Tathāgata’s teaching.
Nor will they take pleasure in the Lokāyata philosophy; beings devoted to poetry will not be pleasing to them;
nor will actors, wrestlers, dancers, nor those who are vintners, butchers, poultry-farmers, pig-breeders, or pimps be pleasing to those beings.
Having heard, written down, retained, or recited such sūtras as these, nothing else will be pleasing to them;
those beings should be known as being endowed with the nature of the Dharma,
and they will possess personal, thorough mental attention (*yoniśomanasikāra*).
Those beings will be supported by the power of their own merit,
and those monks who are holders of such sūtras will be pleasing to behold for all beings.
Passion shall not afflict them,
nor hatred, nor delusion, nor envy, nor stinginess, nor hypocrisy, nor pride, nor arrogance, nor false pride.
And those Dharma-preachers, Samantabhadra, will be content with what they themselves have obtained.

Samantabhadra, in the future time, in the final period, during the last five hundred years, one should generate this thought toward a monk who upholds this Dharma-discourse of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*: "This son of good family will go to the seat of awakening;
this son of good family will conquer the wheel of Māra’s deceit."
He will set in motion the wheel of Dharma; he will beat the drum of Dharma;
he will fill the conch shell of Dharma.
He will rain down the rain of Dharma;
he will ascend the lion-throne of Dharma—
those who, in the final age, in the final time, during the final five hundred years, shall uphold this Dharma-discourse.
Those monks will not be greedy;
they will not be covetous of robes, nor will they be covetous of alms-bowls.
And those Dharma-preachers will be upright.
Furthermore, those Dharma-preachers shall become attainers of the three liberations,
and their own present-life obstacles shall be averted;
yet, for those who harbor delusion toward such monks who are Dharma-preachers and upholders of these sūtras—
Those beings who cause disrepute to be heard regarding monks who uphold such sūtras as these will, in this very life, have variegated bodies and be born blind.
Those who thus deride and mock the scribes of the sūtras will have broken teeth and protruding teeth.
They will have hideous lips,
they will have flat noses,
and they will have deformed hands and feet.
Their eyes will be distorted,
their bodies will emit foul odors, and their bodies will be covered with goiters, boils, scabs, ringworm, and itching.
Those who cause unpleasant words— whether true or false— to be heard by such writers of sūtras, reciters of sūtras, upholders of sūtras, and teachers of sūtras,
their evil karma should be known to be even more grave.
Therefore, Samantabhadra, one should rise from afar to greet the monks who uphold this Dharma discourse.
Just as one should show reverence toward the Tathāgata,
so too should one show such reverence toward those very monks who uphold these sūtras.

Furthermore, while this chapter on the Encouragement of Samantabhadra was being taught, hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, equal in number to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, attained the dhāraṇī known as the "Hundred Thousand-Turn."
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, titled "The Encouragement of Samantabhadra," in the Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.
(Vaidya 268) Chapter 27:
The Entrustment. Then, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, rose from that Dharma-seat.

Having gathered all those bodhisattvas together and, through the perfection of his miraculous power, grasped them by their right hands with his own right hand, he spoke these words at that time: "Sons of good family, I entrust, transmit, deposit, and consign into your hands this unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, which has been accomplished through hundreds of thousands of myriads of kotis of incalculable eons."
"Noble sons, you must act in such a way that it may become vast and widespread.
A second and even a third time, the Blessed One, having taken hold of the entire assembly of bodhisattvas with his right hand, spoke thus.

"O sons of good family, I entrust, hand over, deposit, and consign to your hands this unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, which has been fully accomplished through hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of incalculable eons.
O sons of good family, you must take it up, preserve it, recite it, master it, teach it, and proclaim it."
And it should be proclaimed to all sentient beings:
"O sons of good family, I am free from stinginess; with a mind unattached, I am a fearless giver of the Buddha-knowledge, a giver of the Tathāgata-knowledge and the self-existent knowledge."
“O sons of good family, I am a great master of giving.
You, too, sons of good family, should train yourselves in my very footsteps.

Being free from stinginess, you should proclaim this Dharma discourse to those sons of good family and daughters of good family who have come seeking the vision of the Tathāgata’s knowledge and this great skill in means.”
And those beings who lack faith should be encouraged to take up this Dharma discourse;
in this way, O sons of good family, you will have rendered a service of requital to the Tathāgatas.
When they had been addressed thus by the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas were suffused with great joy and gladness.

Having conceived great reverence, they bowed their bodies toward where the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha was; with their bodies bent low, deeply inclined, and humbled, they lowered their heads, joined their palms in reverence, and with one single voice said:
They said this to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One: "Blessed One, we shall act exactly as the Tathāgata commands;
we shall carry out the command of all the Tathāgatas."
We shall fulfill [them].
May the Blessed One be of little concern and dwell at ease.
A second time [he said]:
For a third time, that entire assembly of bodhisattvas spoke with one voice: "May the Blessed One be free from anxiety and dwell at ease.
We shall act, O Blessed One, exactly as the Tathāgata commands;
we shall fulfill the instructions of all the Tathāgatas."

Then indeed, the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, dismissed all those Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas who had assembled from other world-systems; and he announced to those Tathāgatas that they might dwell as they pleased, saying, "May the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas dwell according to their pleasure."
And he set that jeweled stūpa of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One Prabhūtaratna, back upon its original site;
he also announced to that Tathāgata, Arhat, and Perfectly Enlightened One his dwelling at ease.

The Blessed One spoke thus, and those immeasurable and incalculable Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who had come from other world-systems and were seated upon lion-thrones at the foot of jewel-trees were filled with joy.
The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Prabhūtaratna and that entire host of bodhisattvas—
those immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas headed by Viśiṣṭacāritra who had emerged from the fissures in the earth—
as well as those great śrāvakas and the fourfold assembly.
And the world, including its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, titled "The Entrustment," in the Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.
* * * * * Of those phenomena that arise from causes, the Tathāgata has explained their cause, and also their cessation; such is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa.
